{{Short description|Algebraic theorem}}
In [[algebra]], the '''Milnor–Moore theorem''', introduced by  {{harvs|txt|first1=John W.|last1=Milnor|author1-link=John Milnor|first2=John C.|last2=Moore|author2-link=John Coleman Moore|year=1965}} classifies an important class of [[Hopf algebras]], of the sort that often show up as [[cohomology]] rings in [[algebraic topology]].

The theorem states: given a connected, graded, [[cocommutative]] [[Hopf algebra]] ''A'' over a [[field (mathematics)|field]] of [[characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]] zero with <math>\dim A_n < \infty</math> for all ''n'', the natural Hopf algebra homomorphism
:<math>U(P(A)) \to A</math>
from the [[universal enveloping algebra]] of the graded [[Lie algebra]] <math>P(A)</math> of [[primitive elements (Hopf algebra)|primitive elements]] of ''A'' to ''A'' is an isomorphism. Here we say ''A'' is '''connected''' if <math>A_0</math> is the field and <math>A_n = 0</math> for negative ''n''.  The universal enveloping algebra of a graded Lie algebra ''L'' is the quotient of the [[tensor algebra]] of ''L'' by the two-sided ideal generated by all elements of the form <math>xy- (-1)^{|x||y|}yx - [x,y]</math>.

In [[algebraic topology]], the term usually refers to the corollary of the aforementioned result, that for a [[pointed space|pointed]], [[simply connected space]] ''X'', the following isomorphism holds:
:<math>U(\pi_{\ast}(\Omega X) \otimes \Q) \cong H_{\ast}(\Omega X;\Q),</math>

where <math>\Omega X</math> denotes the [[loop space]] of ''X'', 
compare with Theorem 21.5 from {{harvtxt|Félix|Halperin|Thomas|2001}}. This work may also be compared with that of {{harvs|last=Halpern|year=1958a|year2=1958b}}. Here the multiplication on the right hand side induced by the product <math>\Omega X \times \Omega X \rightarrow \Omega X </math>, and then by the Eilenberg-Zilber multiplication <math>C_*(\Omega X) \times C_*(\Omega X) \rightarrow C_*(\Omega X) </math>.

On the left hand side, since  <math>X</math> is simply connected, <math> \pi_{\ast}(\Omega X) \otimes \Q</math> is a  <math>\Q</math>-vector space; the notation <math>U(V)</math> stands for the universal enveloping algebra.
